edits.html: · G6PD (glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase) makes NADPH (reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate), which keeps glutathione reduced · Without G6PD, sulfonamides and other oxidants cause hemolysis · A sulfonamide can therefore harm a newborn in two ways: albumin displacement, and hemolysis when G6PD is deficient

edits.anchor: leaves the stools yellow and the gallbladder normal.
edits.html:
Unchecked attributePhysiologic jaundice — a total bilirubin of 20 mg/dL exceeds the physiologic peak of about 15, and a hematocrit of 33% points to hemolysis.
True-fact-wrong-slotDehydration — raises indirect bilirubin through enterohepatic reabsorption, but frequent feeds and five stools a day argue against it, and it does not cause anemia.
Salient decoySepsis — can raise indirect bilirubin, but this infant is well on examination; Coombs-negative anemia after an oxidant exposure points to hemolysis.
Salient decoyMilk protein allergy — the cow's milk formula is a decoy; allergy causes reflux, enterocolitis, enteropathy or urticaria, not hemolysis.
